solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My hair is dyed: don't tell Bob, 'e'll be upset!

indicators.note: the contracted 'will be upset' says the words just before it are to be knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, with the apostrophes and comma ignored

explanation.surface: Someone who has secretly coloured their hair begs a friend to keep it from Bob, who would be upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal hides inside the contraction: 'e'll splits into 'e (the cockney he) for the fodder and 'll be upset for the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle blonde is a person whose fair hair comes from a dye bottle rather than nature, so they could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Venomous snake's seen here, by and by?

parts.note: the word by read as its letters: B and Y
the second by read the same way: B and Y

explanation.surface: An idle remark that a dangerous snake will turn up sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out each 'by' letter by letter, joining with 'and': B AND Y, twice. The bandy-bandy is a banded Australian snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandy-bandy is a small venomous Australian snake ringed in black and white bands.

clue.text: My coat is blue: could be bluer with a bit of heliotrope in

indicators.note: 'could be' offers the preceding word as something it might turn into, so its letters are free to move

parts.note: taken as written, as the fodder

indicators.note: only a small piece of the flower name is wanted, and the smallest piece is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of heliotrope

explanation.surface: A creature boasts of its blue coat, which a touch of purple heliotrope could make bluer still.
explanation.walkthrough: The burhel (bharal) is the Himalayan blue sheep, so the first-person definition describes the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The burhel is the Himalayan blue sheep, named for the slate-blue tinge of its wool.

clue.text: End of rot in an acacia, one undergoing termination

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, as something sits in a tree

parts.note: the indefinite article as A
the boree is an Australian acacia tree

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of rot

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon notes that rot at the end of a branch dooms an acacia.
explanation.walkthrough: A boree is an Australian acacia; T goes inside it after the article A.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortee is a person who undergoes an abortion, the termination of a pregnancy.

clue.text: Deny hand needing to work, as one of the smaller farmyard specimens?

definitions.text: one of the smaller farmyard specimens?

indicators.note: letters set to work get busy and move around, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give a hand with the farm work, though a small animal still has to earn its keep.
explanation.walkthrough: Dandy-hen is the Scots word for a bantam hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy-hen is a bantam, a small breed of domestic fowl, hence one of the smaller birds in a farmyard.

clue.text: Black and White (Scotch): sway after tucking into just a little

indicators.note: something tucked into something else ends up inside it

parts.note: a bit is just a little
to sway is to rock

explanation.surface: It reads like a whisky drinker swaying after a small dram of Black and White, a brand of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: Black and White is a Scotch whisky brand; here (Scotch) means the answer is a Scots word for black-and-white.
explanation.definitionFit: Brockit is a Scots word for animals marked in black and white, like a badger, called a brock.

clue.text: The opposite of spring, now early autumn proceeds initially

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the words it follows

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A seasonal note that spring is over and autumn is setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but means a spring tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide is the smallest tide of the month, the opposite of a spring tide, which rises highest.

clue.text: Studies incorporating one Roman and one French saint

indicators.note: to incorporate something is to take it into the body of the whole

parts.note: dens are rooms for study
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A list of reading that covers a Roman saint and a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: St Denis is the patron saint of France, first bishop of Paris.

clue.text: N. American abroad, in point of fact looking up French relative

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: nay used as 'indeed, in fact', as in 'it is good, nay excellent'
qui is the French relative pronoun

explanation.surface: A traveller in America finds, in fact, a French relation doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' is the grammar term, a relative pronoun, not a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanqui is the Spanish form of Yankee, used in Latin America for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Series proceed at too leisurely a pace for nerdy enthusiast?

parts.note: trains are series, as in a train of events

parts.words: proceed at too leisurely a pace
parts.note: to potter is to move along in an idle, unhurried way

explanation.surface: A complaint that some series drag on too slowly for a fan's liking.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is the stock image of a nerdy hobbyist, noting locomotive numbers and, by extension, obsessed with trivia.

clue.text: Cape Town boss, old, one in a bus unusually

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement is one out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one as the article A
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly South African boss rides a bus, which is unusual for a man of his standing.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into A BUS and that is rearranged after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oubaas is Afrikaans for 'old master', a term for a senior man or boss in South Africa.

clue.text: Fish or fruit leaving dock

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the shaddock is the pomelo, a large citrus fruit
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A shipment of fish or fruit departing from the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like the harbour but is the literal letters to be taken away from the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: Scot known for fiction giving his lesson about English

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: lear is a Scots word for learning or a lesson
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Scottish novelist teaches a class on English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Known for fiction' suggests a novelist like Scott, but it means one who tells untruths; 'his' marks lear as a Scots word too.
explanation.definitionFit: Leear is the Scots spelling of liar, someone whose stories are fictions.

clue.text: Rarely seen herb all over local barge

indicators.note: turned all over, the word flips end to end

parts.note: wort is an old word for a plant or herb, now found mainly in compounds

explanation.surface: A rare herb is growing all over a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A trow is a flat-bottomed sailing barge of the River Severn, a regional dialect term.

clue.text: OT text, part of chronicle almost complete, God be praised

indicators.note: almost complete means one short of the whole, so the final letter drops

parts.note: Hos is the abbreviation of Hosea, an Old Testament book
an annal is the record of a single year in a chronicle

explanation.surface: A Bible scholar finishes most of an Old Testament chronicle and gives thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of praise and adoration addressed to God, used in worship.

clue.text: Tired? Cha well brewed acts as a sedative

indicators.note: brewing stirs things together, so the letters are mixed thoroughly

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Feeling weary? A strong pot of tea will calm you down.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Thridace is the inspissated juice of lettuce, formerly given as a mild sedative.

clue.text: NE European making appearance in ballet tights

indicators.note: something making an appearance in a place shows up within it, so look inside the words

parts.note: the end of ballet runs into the start of tights

explanation.surface: A dancer from the Baltic appears on stage in ballet tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lett is a Latvian, a person from the north-eastern European country of Latvia.

clue.text: Aggressive seabird turning like this with cake around?

indicators.note: having another piece around it means one is enclosed by the other
the cake goes around the other piece, enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

indicators.note: turning the short phrase round reads its letters backwards

parts.note: so means like this, in this way

explanation.surface: A bird turns on someone holding a cake, wondering if it should behave like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosun is a dialect name for the great skua, a seabird that bullies other birds into dropping their catch.

clue.text: Edit blue poet being broadcast? (8, two words)

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered too

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A censor is told to cut a smutty poet whose work is going on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests sadness but here means rude, which is why the edit is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleep out is to replace swear words in a broadcast with a tone, a form of editing.

clue.text: After cold, I lie fretting with this? Salve may help it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: fretting means worrying or wearing away, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold lies awake worrying over a sore that ointment might soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheilitis is inflammation of the lips, often cracked and sore, which a soothing balm can ease.

clue.text: Great occasion coming up in summer abroad for shop display

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
one piece placed in the other sits inside it
abroad here means use the foreign word, so the summer is the French one

parts.note: été is French for summer
a gala is a festive occasion

explanation.surface: A big summer event abroad is coming up, so the shops dress their windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Étalage is French for the display of goods in a shop window or on a stall, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Depleted family meeting to discuss ideas

parts.note: a depleted stock is thin
kin are family members

explanation.surface: A shrinking family gathers to talk over its plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A think-in is an informal conference held to brainstorm and exchange ideas.

clue.text: Took a gamble with vicar installed having a special rank

indicators.note: something installed is placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: betted is a past tense of bet
Rev is short for Reverend, the vicar's title

explanation.surface: Someone placed a wager on a vicar being promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet gives an officer a higher honorary rank without the matching pay, so brevetted means holding such a rank.

clue.text: Looking up may identify this garden bush

definitions.meaning: first meaning: improving, as when the outlook gets more hopeful
second meaning: a rose bush, from the French

explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' suggests a reversal in a down clue, but it is a plain definition: things looking up are getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of rosy means more promising, and the noun is a rose tree in the garden.

clue.text: Old scare off with distribution of ration

indicators.note: distributing spreads things out, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Wartime rations are handed out to drive off the hungry crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aroint thee, witch' is Shakespeare's; the word is an archaic command to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroint is an archaic verb meaning to drive away, used chiefly in the imperative.

clue.text: Gaining access with code, rascal grabs $1000

indicators.note: a hand that grabs closes around what it takes

parts.note: a loon is a rogue or idle fellow, in Scottish use
G stands for a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A crook hacks into a system with a password and steals a thousand dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Logon is the act of entering a computer system, typically with a username and password.

clue.text: Bit of sexual harassment, goat's first lunge?

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of goat
a lunge is the long rope used to exercise a horse in a circle

explanation.surface: A lecherous man lunges at someone, an old goat making his first move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunge' looks like a lurch forward but is the horse-trainer's lunging rein.
explanation.definitionFit: A grope is an unwanted sexual touch, a typical act of harassment.

clue.text: Pitches cut up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: Football grounds being dug up and ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a tent is to fix it to the ground, and pins fix things in place.

clue.text: Pen made of bone turned round

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the bone's name runs backwards

parts.note: a rib is a bone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A writing implement carved from bone, as if turned on a lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned round' looks like one phrase, but only 'turned' reverses; 'round' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Biro is the trademark name of the ballpoint pen, used for any such pen.

clue.text: Giants in the main died, being exceptionally large

parts.note: ob. is the abbreviation of obiit, Latin for 'died'
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Huge creatures of the ocean perished because they grew too big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, so the giants are big ships, not monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: OBOs are ore-bulk-oil carriers, very large cargo ships that sail the open sea.

clue.text: By which noose is tightened and top link's broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put back in another order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A rope's noose pulls tight and the top link of the chain snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipknot slides along its own rope, which is how a running noose closes.

clue.text: Head-over-heels in love, head for weepy?

indicators.note: a word turned head over heels is upended so it reads backwards

parts.note: in, turned upside down
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone madly in love, heading for tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head-over-heels in love' reads as one idiom, but splits into a reversal signal, a word and a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobean means like Niobe, the mother in Greek myth who wept endlessly for her slain children.

clue.text: Second outfit required for sudden shower

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
kit is a set of clothing

explanation.surface: A change of clothes is needed after getting caught in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Skit is a Scots and dialect word for a brief, light shower of rain.

clue.text: Part of regiment left behind got drunk when returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: toped is the past tense of tope, to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Soldiers left at base got drunk when the rest came home.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is the part of a regiment that stays at home base, handling recruits, while the rest serves abroad.

clue.text: Passive infinitive in use wrongly, split by participle

indicators.note: something split by another piece has that piece wedged inside it
done wrongly, the letters fall into an incorrect order and must be put right

parts.note: the letters of these words
P is the grammatical abbreviation for participle

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on passive infinitives, used wrongly and split by a participle.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions sit together at the front: supine means passive, and in grammar it is a Latin verbal noun, also a name for the English infinitive with 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine as an adjective means inert and passive; as a grammar term it names an infinitive-like verb form.

clue.text: Looking back, good advice for sluggards?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heraldic term for creatures facing or looking towards each other
second meaning, read cryptically: respect (the) ant, after Proverbs, 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard'

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into two words, an instruction echoing the Bible's advice to idlers to learn from the industrious ant.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, respectant describes two beasts facing each other, each looking back at the other.
